geometry_edits.rationale: Increase the carved court slightly to strengthen public void legibility while preserving the dominant compact mass.
Orient the courtyard opening toward the site access side to improve frontage alignment and ground response.

graph_edits.rationale: Open the courtyard slightly more so the void reads as a clearer public court and not only an internal subtraction.
Align the public opening to the verified access side indicated in program context so the ground threshold is more legible.

rationale: The candidate reads as a single compact mass in all four views, with a coherent stepped upper volume and a carved central void. It responds reasonably to the parcel boundary rather than just filling the box, and the form is not visibly self-colliding across views. The main weakness is that the public void is still fairly small/abstract and the frontage response to the verified access edge is only lightly legible, so the neighborhood-living brief is supported but not strongly articulated. The section is acceptable for an early massing study, though it would benefit from a clearer ground threshold or entry carve aligned to the access side.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a taller tower typology; transfer the mass hierarchy and section clarity, not the height or skyline objectness.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact mixed-use mass with a clear tapered/stepped upper condition can support a legible dominant volume without losing urban presence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is low-rise and courtyard-based, so the tower proportion and riverfront context are not directly transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A subtly curved or slumped vertical profile can soften a stacked mass while preserving a single dominant read.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more explicitly retail/cafe at ground level; use only the threshold logic, not the signage or frontage styling.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low horizontal base with a legible canopy/threshold and a compact upper element can express active ground interface for neighborhood program.

warnings: The access-edge response is present but weak; the mass should open more explicitly toward the verified road frontage.
The void reads more as an internal cut than a clearly public court/entry seam.
If further refined, preserve the dominant compact stepped gesture and avoid fragmenting the single-mass read.
